title: [Refurb] Dell OptiPlex 7090 Micro PC: i5-11500T, 16GB RAM, 256GB SSD $369.75 ($361.05 eBay Plus) Del @ Aust Computer Trader eBay
body:
Deal: [Refurb] Dell OptiPlex 7090 Micro PC: i5-11500T, 16GB RAM, 256GB SSD $369.75 ($361.05 eBay Plus) Del @ Aust Computer Trader eBay

[3dprintdeals] Perfect for minilabs in 10" 3D printed racks.
[bleeder] Can confirm, I have a cluster with 2 of these and a HP Elite Book (which doesn't fit in the 10" rack)
[spasticspeaker] Do these use SODIMM? If I wanted to get more RAM in each, would that be difficult these days?
[3dprintdeals] They have two DIMM slots.
The unit will come with 1x16gb
https://www.dell.com/support/manuals/en-au/optiplex-7090-mic…
[Johnsnu] Yes, they use SODIMM. It has 2 slots. If it's just 1 16GB stick, easier to upgrade. If it comes with 2 x 8GB sticks, going to bit more difficult.
I managed to get a 16GB off FB Marketplace, same brand and speed as the one already inside, for $55. Brand new, more in the range of ~$130.
[Badger2066] @Johnsnu: You sure they're SODIMM and not just DIMM? SODIMM is for laptops usually.
[3dprintdeals] @Badger2066: Yes, SODIMM it's 1L formfactor
[B-Moose] Any link to the best mini rack option? Any ready made to buy? Otherwise can find someone to print.
[3dprintdeals] Start LabRax and go from there
DM for printing info. I'm not in Melbourne but can send you some contacts.
[sloshie] There's also the 10th gen 10500T model for $331 (ebayPlus) (although only 2 available) or there was a 512Gb SSD 11th Gen 11500T model for $20 more than the one linked in this deal, but appeared to be only 1 of those available (and now none by the time I posted this).
[macmanluke] Its interesting how well these hold there value
I have a few 24inch Dell AIOs with 10500 8GB 512GB SSD win11 which im trying to move after accidentally winning more than i need at a local auction and cant seem to get any interest even well under $300
[jonathonsunshine] Might be the monitor holding it back, I think most people who buys this on OzBargain are connecting to their TV or it's gonna sit in a cupboard without a monitor attached at all, IE, JellyFin and the Arrs.
[dontpanic] This is absolutely it. These are popular because they tick every box - cheap, small, energy efficient and powerful enough to run a headless Proxmox homelab.
[3dprintdeals] These 1L units are sought after for homelab
[60beetle60] @carrawa: 1 Litre, volume of case. Very small PC's
[carrawa] @60beetle60: Thanks. I would never have associated it with 1L.
[3dprintdeals] @carrawa: The volume
Dell OptiPlex Micro
Lenovo ThinkCentre Tiny
HP EliteDesk Mini
HP ProDesk Mini
[adrianhughes1998] Wonder if this would be good to be a NAS, instead of buying an actual NAS?
[tonyjzx] at most you have one nmve and one sata so if you want to buy a das it would be ok but you can use a vastly cheaper usff pc to do the same… even something like 4th gen and sub $100 would be fine
[adrianhughes1998] Thank you, yeh thinking about a small always on setup cos NAS is expensive. Well moreso the hard drives that go in..
[Larsson] Pcie lanes are the issue. Depending on the array you are planning, it is at best inconvenient. But doable, there are plenty of 3D printed enclosures just to do that.
[Ashh77] Is this overkill to run HA, plex server? If I need more storage do I need to purchase additional ssd?
Absolutely new to media servers and HA however would love to learn.
[tonyjzx] unless you can fit all your shit on 256gb then of course you need HDDs or an array
this thing is fast enough for a HA and plex except perhaps on video but i think onboard is quite good
[LuckyLuke] I have an NVIDIA shield pro with a external Samsung T7 portable SSD plugged in for storage. It works perfectly. It takes a little bit of setting up and some learning to be able to remotely put content on the drive, but it works great and sits behind the tv, so you wouldn't know it was there.
[sparx971] Do you have a link explaining how to remotely put content on the drive? I have the same setup and would love to be able to do that. Do you use Plex?
[sparx971] @3dprintdeals: Thanks mate I'll look into that
[loksmack] 256gb is fine for the OS and apps.
Your media will live on external drives probably in a DAS enclosure.
The alternative route is to buy a NAS and run Plex Server and HA directly on it.
[Ashh77] Makes sense! Overall goal is a bit of learning accross networking, HA and managing a media server. Will look into additional storage down the line.
[hollykryten] Yes it is as it's only an office PC. I don't think anyone's going to be using this for gaming so no need for a large internal storage.
[willyroo] Running a pretty decent HA setup on a 7070. Includes 700+ line yaml for solar, batteries, pool, HWS, EV charging etc.
Plex? See above.
[FujinShu] If you already have a nas based on old hardware, you can just buy this and save compute in your nas for storage-only tasks while this handles everything else.
[wisc] Except for electricity having two units running 24/7
To make round numbers, even at less than 100 watts, let's say 2kw per day, it's like 50c a day to run. (Assuming 25kw for electricity)
Over a year its 180 a year to run…. Better off putting in extra and getting a dedicated low power unit, it will pay for itself over the life of the unit.
Real world Idle should be far less electricity, but you get the idea..
(Maybe 20% of that so still looking at 50 bux or so…a year to run extra hardware, if the device will run for 5 years that's still 250 bux… Better if spend on a single dedicated unit)
[pinkybrain] which dedicated unit you referring to and how much it cost compared to this?
[FujinShu] Well you can always just lower the power usage by having less programs running on your nas, which is what this should help with.
[cevad] I use one of these (but a 12500t cpu) as a Plex server and it's amazing. I have Plexpass (have had it for years), and it transcodes multiple streams at once.
I have all of my media on NAS set up with NFS (the Dell is running Linux).
[pinkybrain] how much you paid for it?
what total spec of machie?
how it compares to 11500t ?
[warmmilktea] New to media too I was about to buy ugoos, but this seems quite good , sorry for my noobness what is HA?
[paulied84] Thanks OP bought 1 to add to my Proxmox cluster.
[Johnsnu] I've purchased 2 different refurb 7090s from past deals. One had the one 16GB stick and the other 2 8GB sticks, which made it harder to upgrade the RAM since both slots were now taken. Couldn't find a mention of it in this listing.
[CrushJelly] Great for HA. I have my setup on a 7090.
[3dprintdeals] You can do a lot more than HA with one.
Run it as a VM on Proxmox, LXCs, other VMs…
[paulied84] Yep 100%. I run HAOS as a VM and heaps of other lxc's.
They're great little devices which have low power draw.
[pinkybrain] what is the recommend storage size for proxmox machine and size for HA as a VM?
what other VMs you got running?
what is LXC?
[3dprintdeals] @pinkybrain: I have 256 in mine, and it's running:
Opnsense
HA
Adguard LXC
Ubuntu VM
It really depends on how much you want to store on it, I store everything on NAS.
An LXC is a lightweight Linux VM that shares the Proxmox host’s kernel.
[pinkybrain] @3dprintdeals:
I have 256 in mine, and it's running:
so no
jellyfin or Immich on same machine?
how you backing up your photos?

[koven] The SFF version as opposed to the micro has 3.5" hdd and 4 ram slots
[3dprintdeals] SFF version doesn't fit in a 10" rack and takes up more space if making a cluster.
Two also fit side by side in a 19" rack
There are reasons why people want the 1L form factor.
[ReaperX22] Yessss. I've got a deskpi T0 with a 7080 optiplex and a 3d printed mount, ucg fiber 3d printed mount and a keystone jack both sides + another 3d mounted ubiquiti poe switch. It's so good. And so much easier to move around. Especially when we move (we rent), instead of a bajillion cables, it's basically just 2-3 now in and we're off/set back up again.
I also bought the deeper T0 version but currently it just holds my 4 bay synology nas so it all looks more matchy matchy ha
[koven] The SFF also has pcie slot for 2.5 or 10gbe network card
[ReaperX22] You can generally convert the M.2 WiFi card slots with a pcie card off aliexpress to a 2.5gb nic though (just make sure you get an Intel one)
[cevad] this is what I've done :)
Realek 2.5Gb pcie works fine, cheaper than an Intel one.
[ReaperX22] @cevad: Depends on the use case.
Proxmox/Linux just generally works better (or at least, more consistently, with Intel nics over realtek or mediatek). Not saying realtek won't work but kind of a tried and true thing
[3dprintdeals] @ReaperX22: Running M.2 2.5gbe realtek nic for over a year with opnsense
[cevad] @ReaperX22: I've not had any issues with a RTL8125 2.5GbE m.2 with Linux for a couple of years.
[pinkybrain] got a link for aliexpress?
so these do not have ethernet?
[cevad] @pinkybrain: they have Gigabit Intel I219-LM Ethernet built in.
Nah, I bought mine so long ago the link in my account is dead lol
It was something like this one - https://www.aliexpress.com/item/1005006895983767.html just make sure you get the right one
[3dprintdeals] I added a 2.5gbe nic to mine using m.2 card - realtek
Works fine for opnsense
[eraser215] I have a Dell precision with the i7-12700 and it still only has 2 so-dimm slots.
[BenTheBargainer2013] Thanks op, bought the 7080 yesterday for much more, hopefully they let me return it (same seller)
[Blizzard57] Does anyone know if these come with windows 11 Pro or home?
[ReaperX22] Almost all of these ex office or whatever refurbs will have a pro license attached to them. Otherwise they couldn't really be fleet managed properly by whatever org had them before
[Blizzard57] Thanks! Asked the seller and they said it comes with variations of home or pro and will do their best to give me Pro. Best yeah, I agree, I would imagine that would mostly come with pro as they are ex office.
[tanksinatra] Just be aware that these use T series CPU's which are capped at 35W. That can limit performance under sustained workloads.

Cpu differences - 11500t vs 10500t

[jedimaster] I use an older HP elitedesk g2 micro pc with i5-6500T woth 16GB ram as my plex server. Its connect to a Sabrent 4 x 2.5" DOCK over usb with each slot having 4 x 4 TB SATA SSD. Internal storage is another 4TB sata ssd and 1TB NVMe for OS. Works great
[Jeff1001] two boxes, high risks for disconnection and high power consumption, why not use a SFF only, it supports 3-4 SATA and you can buy a card for pci to another 4 SATA, lower cost and better performance.
